text: dsh-web-lan-access 为 DSH Web 提供局域网和远程访问。bundle patch 用支持通配绑定的服务替代内置 webserver，并注入 Host ownership bootstrap。它可监听所有网卡、从非内部 IPv4 生成 trustedHosts、让远程页面使用 Host 设置，并为通配监听生成可拨号的 origin。适合从局域网、Tailscale 或 VPN 访问 DSH Web；无需 API key 或外部账号。

dsh-web-lan-access lets you reach DSH Web over LAN, Tailscale, or VPN. Its patch mounts a wildcard-capable webserver, trusts active non-internal IPv4 addresses, injects a Host ownership bootstrap, and maps wildcard origins to loopback. No API key or external account is needed.
想从同一个局域网里的另一台电脑打开 DSH Web。
有没有办法在手机浏览器里看家里电脑运行的 DSH？
让 DSH Web 通过 Tailscale 地址也能访问。
远程打开页面后，希望模型和 Host 设置也能正常显示。
我想从 VPN 网卡的 IP 访问 DSH 界面。
DSH 网页只能本机打开，怎么让其他设备连进来？
Make my DSH Web interface reachable from another device on my LAN.
I need to access the DSH web UI over my Tailscale network.
dsh-web-lan-access 的功能「通配绑定」：替代内置 webserver，允许绑定 0.0.0.0 或 ::，并保留原 schema 的其余校验。端口和 TLS 配置仍由启动参数提供。
dsh-web-lan-access 的功能「网卡地址信任」：patch 从当前非内部 IPv4 地址生成 trustedHosts，供已启动的局域网、Tailscale 或 VPN 网卡访问使用。
dsh-web-lan-access 的功能「Host bootstrap」：index tap 在 head 前部注入 ownsHost 标记并保留 fetch；已有 shell transport 时不覆盖。
dsh-web-lan-access 的功能「服务 origin」：通配绑定返回回环地址，IPv6 地址加方括号，getOrigin 提供当前协议、主机和端口组成的 URL。
dsh-web-lan-access 使用前须知：自动生成的 trustedHosts 只取非内部 IPv4 地址，不包含 MagicDNS 主机名；按主机名访问时需另行添加 --trusted-host。
dsh-web-lan-access 使用前须知：bundle 的网卡地址表达式使用 process.getBuiltinModule，patch 注释标明此接口要求 Node.js 22.3 或更高版本。

dsh-web-lan-access README · dsh-web-lan-access：[](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

LAN / remote access support for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web UI.

Bind every interface with one command, reach the GUI from a LAN IP, a Tailscale IP, or a VPN address, and keep Host-backed settings working on the remote page.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Compatibility：| dsh | plugin | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **0.2.2-rc.1** | **1.4.x** | current; verified end to end |
| 0.2.1-rc.x | 1.4.x | verified end to end |
| 0.2.0-rc.x | 1.3.x | shipped webserver still accepted `0.0.0.0` |
| ≤ 0.1.7 | 1.3.x | no wildcard ban yet |

Version 1.4.0 is the release that tracks dsh 0.2.1's stricter webserver. See [Why 1.4.0 had to change](#why-140-had-to-change) if you are upgrading from 1.3.x.

dsh-web-lan-access README · The problem：Three separate things stand between a remote browser and a working GUI:

**1. The listener binds loopback only.** `dsh web` defaults to `127.0.0.1`, and from 0.2.1 the CLI rejects a wildcard host outright:

```
error: --host 0.0.0.0 is an unspecified (wildcard) address, which is not supported:
binding every interface would expose remote code execution to the network
```

dsh-web-lan-access README · The problem：**2. The `/api` fence rejects unknown authorities.** Every request must name a loopback host, the listener's own bind literal, or a declared `trustedHosts` entry. A wildcard bind has no literal of its own — `0.0.0.0` matches no request `Host` — so the page shell loads but every `/api` call returns **403** and sessions never appear.

dsh-web-lan-access README · The problem：**3. Host-backed settings are gated on `isLoopback`.** `client-connection` derives `isLoopback: transport?.ownsHost === true`, and client plugins consult that fact before reaching Host surfaces. A page served from a LAN or Tailscale address is not loopback by hostname, so the Models and plugin settings pages stay empty even after authentication succeeds.
dsh-web-lan-access README · The fix：Two small pieces, both reversible.
dsh-web-lan-access README · A replacement `webserver` row：`lib/webserver.js` subclasses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` and changes exactly two things:

dsh-web-lan-access README · A replacement `webserver` row：- **`Config`** delegates to the shipped schema and rescues *only* the wildcard rejection. A non-literal host, a port out of range, or a missing port still fail exactly as before — the relaxation is one error message wide.
- **`getOrigin()`** never returns a wildcard origin. The parent builds its URL from the bind address, which would yield `http://0.0.0.0:3080` — an address no browser can dial. A wildcard listener reports loopback instead, and `--public-url` still overrides the advertised root upstream.
dsh-web-lan-access README · A replacement `webserver` row：Everything else — the service name, routes, index taps, TLS handling, gzip, listener lifecycle — is inherited untouched.

dsh-web-lan-access README · A `/api` fence widened from the live interface list：The bundle patch derives `trustedHosts` from every non-internal IPv4 the host currently has, so LAN, Tailscale (`100.x`), and VPN addresses are all accepted without per-IP configuration.
section: A `/api` fence widened from the live interface list

text: dsh-web-lan-access README · A bootstrap script for Host ownership：Injected as the first script in `<head>`, before the boot manifest and shell entry, through the webserver's official index-tap extension point (`webServer.tapIndex`). It declares `ownsHost: true` while keeping the ordinary HTTP `fetch` transport, and leaves a transport supplied by another shell untouched.
section: A bootstrap script for Host ownership

text: dsh-web-lan-access README · A bootstrap script for Host ownership：> **What 1.4.0 removed:** the `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill. From 0.2.1 DSH mints UUIDs through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-util-crypto`, which is built on `crypto.getRandomValues` — available on insecure origins — so a plain-HTTP LAN page needs no patch to render. The old polyfill is gone because the bug it worked around no longer exists.
section: A bootstrap script for Host ownership

dsh-web-lan-access README · Why 1.4.0 had to change：Through 1.3.x this plugin worked by writing `host: '0.0.0.0'` into the shipped `webserver` row's config. That stopped working in 0.2.1 for two independent reasons:

1. The webserver's own schema now rejects wildcard addresses, so the row fails validation and the boot aborts with `3 required plugins did not activate`.
2. A patch cannot retarget a row's `name` — app-boot skips any patch whose `name` differs from the target's — so the row could not be swapped for a custom module in place.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Why 1.4.0 had to change：1.4.0 therefore disables the shipped row (`disabled: true`, which startup auditing skips) and mounts the subclass under a new id. A second breakage came from the same upgrade: `web-app` no longer provides the `webRuntime` service, so the old `ctx.webRuntime?.trustedHosts` expression threw `cannot get property "webRuntime" without inject`. The fence list is now derived directly from `os.networkInterfaces()`.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Method 1: Ask your DSH Agent (Easiest 🤖)：Send this repo URL directly to your DSH chat with the instruction:
> "Install this plugin for me: https://github.com/AcidGr/dsh-web-lan-access"

Your DSH Agent will automatically install the package and configure it in the background.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Method 2: Bundle install via CLI (Recommended)：From npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-web-lan-access
```

From the repo (no npm publish / local development):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:AcidGr/dsh-web-lan-access
```

Restart `dsh web`, then hard-refresh the browser.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Method 3: Manual install (no pnpm / offline)：```sh
PROFILE="$DSH_HOME/profiles/web"                 # adjust DSH_HOME and profile name
mkdir -p "$PROFILE/plugins"
cp -r dsh-web-lan-access "$PROFILE/plugins/lan-access"
ln -sfn ../../plugins/lan-access "$PROFILE/node_modules/dsh-web-lan-access"

Then add `dsh-web-lan-access` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` in `package.json`. The bundle patch registers its own rows, so no manual `cordis.patch.yml` edit is needed.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Usage：The plugin is **self-contained**: the bundle patch supplies the bind host, so you do **not** pass `--host` (and must not — the CLI still rejects `0.0.0.0`). `--port`, `--tls-cert`, `--tls-key`, and `--public-url` all still work.

1. **Install the plugin, then start normally:**

```sh
   dsh --profile web --port 3080
   ```

dsh-web-lan-access README · Usage：The patch derives the `/api` fence from **every non-internal IPv4** the host currently has — LAN (`192.168.x`), **Tailscale (`100.x`)**, and VPN interfaces. As long as the remote interface is up when `dsh web` starts, **LAN and Tailscale IP access need zero extra config**: open `http://<server-ip>:3080` or `http://<tailscale-ip>:3080` and sessions and models load.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Usage：> If you would rather not let the plugin take over the bind host (for example you want loopback plus a port forward), remove the `dsh-web-lan-access` bundle and forward a port (socat / rinetd / `tailscale serve`) from `127.0.0.1:3080`, adding the forwarded address to `trustedHosts` manually.

2. **MagicDNS hostnames (e.g. `xxx.tailXXXX.ts.net`)** — the fence discovers IP literals only, never hostnames. Add your own names when you browse by name rather than by IP, using the repeatable CLI flag:

dsh-web-lan-access README · Usage：```sh
   dsh --profile web --trusted-host myhost --trusted-host myhost.tailXXXX.ts.net
   ```

Or replace the `connection` row's `trustedHosts` with a literal list that still includes the interface addresses:

```yaml
   - id: connection
     config:
       trustedHosts:
         - <short-name>            # e.g. myhost — MUST be listed separately!

dsh-web-lan-access README · Usage：⚠️ The fence compares the `Host` header **literally**: a MagicDNS short name (`http://myhost:3080`) is *not* the full domain — list the short name on its own line, or every `/api` call returns 403 (page shell loads, sessions and models absent).

> ⚠️ A literal list on `connection.config.trustedHosts` **replaces** the bundle's derived expression rather than merging with it. Either keep the derived expression and add names with `--trusted-host`, or spell out every IP you need. Do not mix the two.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Host ownership scope：The transport signal enables every client surface DSH associates with owning the Host, not only Models. That includes Host-backed settings and native Host actions such as opening a produced file. Use this plugin only when the authenticated remote browser is meant to operate the agent machine. DSH's Host/Origin fence and browser authentication remain in force; this signal changes the client's capability projection, not request authentication.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Host ownership scope：Older harness builds that pin privileged methods to loopback on the server continue returning 403 for those methods. This client bootstrap does not weaken that server-side fence.
dsh-web-lan-access README · Verify：```sh
dsh-web-lan-access README · 1. the bootstrap is injected：curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3080/ -b <cookie> | grep lan-access-bootstrap
dsh-web-lan-access README · 2. every interface is listening (0.0.0.0 in the address column)：ss -ltnp | grep 3080
section: 2. every interface is listening (0.0.0.0 in the address column)

text:
dsh-web-lan-access README · 3. the fence admits your interface IPs and refuses anything else：curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "Host: 100.64.0.5:3080" http://127.0.0.1:3080/api  # 401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "Host: evil.example:3080" http://127.0.0.1:3080/api  # 403
```

`401` means the fence admitted the authority and only the session cookie is missing — that is the expected result for a trusted IP without a browser session. `403` means the authority was rejected. Then open `http://<server-ip>:3080` from another device: sessions and models must load.
section: 3. the fence admits your interface IPs and refuses anything else

dsh-web-lan-access README · Security warning：Binding `0.0.0.0` exposes the DSH authentication surface to **every** reachable interface, including addresses you may not have considered — container bridges, VPN tunnels, and any other network the host is attached to. `trustedHosts` is an Origin/Host fence, not identity; DSH separately authenticates the browser.

This plugin deliberately relaxes a restriction the DSH maintainers added on purpose:

> binding every interface would expose remote code execution to the network

dsh-web-lan-access README · Security warning：Use it only on trusted networks, restrict the port with a firewall (e.g. `ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16`), or front it with Tailscale or an authenticated reverse proxy. If a single interface is enough, prefer plain `dsh web --host <ip>` — it needs no plugin, and the fence auto-trusts the bind literal.

Because this plugin depends on the webserver's schema and URL-building internals, a future DSH release may break it again. Check the compatibility table before upgrading.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Rollback：- Bundle install: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-web-lan-access`
- Manual install: remove `dsh-web-lan-access` from `dsh.profile.bundles`; the bundle patch's rows disappear with it and the shipped loopback-only `webserver` takes over again.

dsh-web-lan-access README · Development：```sh
node --test        # 9 tests, no dependencies beyond the linked dsh packages
```

`lib/webserver.js` needs `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` resolvable from the package root. When developing outside a profile, link it once:

```sh
mkdir -p node_modules/@deepseek-ai
ln -sfn "$(npm root -g)/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver" \
        node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver
```
